plan.goal: Deepen the selected idea, De-Smoothed Perplexity, into a stronger research proposal.

args.instruction: Deepen the selected idea 'De-Smoothed Perplexity: Score the Sharp Component, Not the Injected Floor'. Work through its load-bearing assumption (that train and eval targets are identical / that raw probabilities are comparable across training schemes) and its open questions, and turn the proposal into something more defensible and concrete: (1) resolve or bound the clipping bias when p(y) falls below the uniform floor alpha/K — is the relu-renormalize transform biased for genuinely uncertain predictions, and can a floor-adjusted likelihood or an alternative transform avoid that; (2) decide whether evaluation should use the training alpha or fit alpha on held-out data, and how to make that choice principled; (3) check whether the de-smoothed distribution is a proper scoring rule and what happens to decoding/beam-search rankings if it is used; (4) address what a residual gap after de-smoothing means — real degradation vs a temperature/calibration shift caused by smoothing, and how to disentangle them; (5) make the evaluation protocol concrete against named baselines, including the inverse-mixture correction q=(p-alpha*u)/(1-alpha) used in the sibling annealed-smoothing idea, and state what evidence would confirm or falsify the claim that de-smoothed PPL tracks BLEU/accuracy better than raw PPL. Keep the idea's core move — leaving training untouched and fixing the evaluation premise — but tighten its weakest parts.

steps.why: The user wants the selected idea pushed further; that is refinement of one idea already in context.

done_criteria: at least one refined version of the idea returned
the refined version addresses the open questions: clipping bias, fitted vs training alpha, proper scoring / decoding, and residual-gap interpretation
